You want to improve the accuracy of the model when predicting new data. What should you do?
answers: Increase the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features
Increase the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features
Reduce the size of the training dataset, and increase the number of input features
Reduce the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features
correct_answer: Increase the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Increase the size of the training dataset, and decrease the number of input features]**: Aumentar el tamaño del conjunto de datos de entrenamiento y reducir el número de características de entrada ayuda a reducir el overfitting. Esto permite que el modelo aprenda de más ejemplos y evita que se concentre en patrones irrelevantes o ruido en los datos.
- **:red[Increase training size, increase features]**: Aumentar las características podría agravar el problema de overfitting.
- **:red[Reduce training size, increase features]**: Esta combinación podría empeorar el overfitting al proporcionar menos datos y más características.
- **:red[Reduce training size, decrease features]**: Reducir el tamaño del conjunto de datos probablemente empeoraría el problema de overfitting.

question: You are implementing a chatbot to help an online retailer streamline their customer service. The chatbot must be able to respond to both text and voice inquiries. You are looking for a low-code or no-code option, and you want to be able to easily train the chatbot to provide answers to keywords. What should you do?
answers: Use the Cloud Speech-to-Text API to build a Python application in App Engine
Use the Cloud Speech-to-Text API to build a Python application in a Compute Engine instance
Use Dialogflow for simple queries and the Cloud Speech-to-Text API for complex queries
Use Dialogflow to implement the chatbot, defining the intents based on the most common queries collected
correct_answer: Use Dialogflow to implement the chatbot, defining the intents based on the most common queries collected
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use Dialogflow to implement the chatbot]**: Dialogflow es una plataforma de Google Cloud para construir interfaces conversacionales como chatbots, lo que permite implementar de manera sencilla un chatbot que soporte texto y voz.
- **:red[Use Speech-to-Text API on App Engine]**: Requiere más desarrollo de código y solo aborda la parte de voz a texto.
- **:red[Speech-to-Text API on Compute Engine]**: No proporciona una solución completa para un chatbot, además requiere más gestión de infraestructura.
- **:red[Dialogflow for simple queries, Speech-to-Text for complex ones]**: Introduce innecesariamente dos sistemas separados cuando Dialogflow puede manejar ambos tipos de entradas.

question: An aerospace company uses a proprietary data format to store its flight data. You need to connect this new data source to BigQuery and stream the data into BigQuery. You want to efficiently import the data into BigQuery while consuming as few resources as possible. What should you do?
answers: Write a shell script that triggers a Cloud Function that performs periodic ETL batch jobs on the new data source
Use a standard Dataflow pipeline to store the raw data in BigQuery, and then transform the format later when the data is used
Use Apache Hive to write a Dataproc job that streams the data into BigQuery in CSV format
Use an Apache Beam custom connector to write a Dataflow pipeline that streams the data into BigQuery in Avro format
correct_answer: Use an Apache Beam custom connector to write a Dataflow pipeline that streams the data into BigQuery in Avro format
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Apache Beam custom connector with Dataflow pipeline]**: Beam permite crear conectores personalizados para manejar formatos de datos propietarios y, junto con Dataflow, permite realizar un streaming eficiente de datos en tiempo real a BigQuery utilizando el formato Avro.
- **:red[Cloud Function and ETL batch jobs]**: No cumple con el requisito de streaming de datos en tiempo real.
- **:red[Standard Dataflow pipeline, raw data]**: Transformar los datos más tarde puede ser ineficiente y costoso a largo plazo.
- **:red[Apache Hive with Dataproc, CSV]**: CSV no es un formato eficiente para almacenamiento o transmisión de datos, y Dataproc está más orientado a procesamiento por lotes.

question: An online brokerage company requires a high volume trade processing architecture. You need to create a secure queuing system that triggers jobs. The jobs will run in Google Cloud and call the company's Python API to execute trades. You need to efficiently implement a solution. What should you do?
answers: Use a Pub/Sub push subscription to trigger a Cloud Function to pass the data to the Python API
Write an application hosted on a Compute Engine instance that makes a push subscription to the Pub/Sub topic
Write an application that makes a queue in a NoSQL database
Use Cloud Composer to subscribe to a Pub/Sub topic and call the Python API
correct_answer: Use a Pub/Sub push subscription to trigger a Cloud Function to pass the data to the Python API
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Pub/Sub push subscription with Cloud Function]**: Pub/Sub proporciona un sistema de mensajería escalable para manejar altos volúmenes de mensajes, y Cloud Functions permite ejecutar código Python sin necesidad de gestionar infraestructura.
- **:red[Compute Engine with push subscription]**: Requiere más gestión de infraestructura y es menos eficiente que una solución serverless.
- **:red[NoSQL database queue]**: Añade complejidad innecesaria al no aprovechar servicios gestionados.
- **:red[Cloud Composer]**: Es más adecuado para orquestar flujos de trabajo complejos, no para procesamiento de transacciones en tiempo real.

question: Your company wants to be able to retrieve large result sets of medical information from your current system, which has over 10 TBs in the database, and store the data in new tables for further query. The database must have a low-maintenance architecture and be accessible via SQL. You need to implement a cost-effective solution that can support data analytics for large result sets. What should you do?
answers: Use Cloud SQL, but first organize the data into tables. Use JOIN in queries to retrieve data
Use BigQuery as a data warehouse. Set output destinations for caching large queries
Use a MySQL cluster installed on a Compute Engine managed instance group for scalability
Use Cloud Spanner to replicate the data across regions. Normalize the data in a series of tables
correct_answer: Use BigQuery as a data warehouse. Set output destinations for caching large queries
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use BigQuery as a data warehouse]**: BigQuery es una solución rentable y escalable para grandes volúmenes de datos, compatible con SQL y con una arquitectura de bajo mantenimiento. Ofrece un buen rendimiento para conjuntos de datos de más de 10 TB.
- **:red[Cloud SQL with JOINs]**: Puede ser ineficiente y no escalar adecuadamente para conjuntos de datos tan grandes.
- **:red[MySQL cluster on Compute Engine]**: Requiere más gestión de infraestructura, lo que va en contra del requisito de bajo mantenimiento.
- **:red[Cloud Spanner]**: Aunque es potente, es más costoso y puede ser excesivo para este caso de uso.

question: You have 15 TB of data in your on-premises data center that you want to transfer to Google Cloud. Your data changes weekly and is stored in a POSIX-compliant source. The network operations team has granted you 500 Mbps bandwidth to the public internet. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to reliably transfer your data to Google Cloud on a weekly basis. What should you do?
answers: Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger the gsutil command. Use the -m parameter for optimal parallelism
Use Transfer Appliance to migrate your data into a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster, and then configure a weekly transfer job
Install Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data in your data center, and then configure a weekly transfer job
Install Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data on a Google Cloud virtual machine, and then configure a weekly transfer job
correct_answer: Install Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data in your data center, and then configure a weekly transfer job
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Install Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data]**: Es la solución recomendada por Google para grandes volúmenes de datos que requieren transferencias recurrentes. Permite programar trabajos semanales y está optimizado para maximizar el uso de ancho de banda disponible.
- **:red[Use Cloud Scheduler and gsutil]**: gsutil no está optimizado para transferencias recurrentes de grandes volúmenes de datos.
- **:red[Transfer Appliance and GKE]**: Transfer Appliance es adecuado para migraciones únicas, no para transferencias recurrentes.
- **:red[Storage Transfer on a Google Cloud VM]**: Esta opción requiere una etapa adicional de transferir los datos primero a la nube, lo que no es eficiente para actualizaciones semanales.

question: You are designing a system that requires an ACID-compliant database. You must ensure that the system requires minimal human intervention in case of a failure. What should you do?
answers: Configure a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance with point-in-time recovery enabled
Configure a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance with high availability enabled
Configure a Bigtable instance with more than one cluster
Configure a BigQuery table with a multi-region configuration
correct_answer: Configure a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance with high availability enabled
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with high availability]**: PostgreSQL cumple con las propiedades ACID, y la configuración de alta disponibilidad ofrece replicación síncrona y conmutación por error automática, minimizando la intervención humana en caso de fallo.
- **:red[Cloud SQL for MySQL with point-in-time recovery]**: Aunque útil, la recuperación puntual no aborda la alta disponibilidad requerida.
- **:red[Bigtable with multiple clusters]**: Bigtable no es ACID-compliant.
- **:red[BigQuery multi-region configuration]**: BigQuery no está diseñado para operaciones transaccionales que requieren ACID.

question: You are implementing workflow pipeline scheduling using open source-based tools and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You want to use a Google managed service to simplify and automate the task. You also want to accommodate Shared VPC networking considerations. What should you do?
answers: Use Dataflow for your workflow pipelines. Use Cloud Run triggers for scheduling
Use Dataflow for your workflow pipelines. Use shell scripts to schedule workflows
Use Cloud Composer in a Shared VPC configuration. Place the Cloud Composer resources in the host project
Use Cloud Composer in a Shared VPC configuration. Place the Cloud Composer resources in the service project
correct_answer: Use Cloud Composer in a Shared VPC configuration. Place the Cloud Composer resources in the service project
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Cloud Composer in Shared VPC, service project]**: Cloud Composer es ideal para la orquestación de flujos de trabajo y se integra con GKE. Colocar los recursos en el proyecto de servicio sigue las mejores prácticas de Google para Shared VPC.
- **:red[Dataflow and Cloud Run]**: Dataflow está diseñado para procesamiento de datos, no para orquestación de flujos de trabajo.
- **:red[Dataflow and shell scripts]**: No proporciona la robustez necesaria para flujos de trabajo complejos.
- **:red[Composer in host project]**: No es la mejor práctica colocar los recursos de Cloud Composer en el proyecto host.

question: You are using BigQuery and Data Studio to design a customer-facing dashboard that displays large quantities of aggregated data. You expect a high volume of concurrent users. You need to optimize the dashboard to provide quick visualizations with minimal latency. What should you do?
answers: Use BigQuery BI Engine with materialized views
Use BigQuery BI Engine with logical views
Use BigQuery BI Engine with streaming data
Use BigQuery BI Engine with authorized views
correct_answer: Use BigQuery BI Engine with materialized views
explanation:
- **✅:green[ BigQuery BI Engine with materialized views]**: BI Engine acelera las consultas en memoria, y las vistas materializadas proporcionan datos precalculados para consultas rápidas, reduciendo significativamente la latencia.
- **:red[BI Engine with logical views]**: Las vistas lógicas no ofrecen el mismo rendimiento que las materializadas.
- **:red[BI Engine with streaming data]**: No es adecuado para grandes cantidades de datos agregados.
- **:red[BI Engine with authorized views]**: Las vistas autorizadas controlan el acceso a los datos, no optimizan el rendimiento.

question: Government regulations in the banking industry mandate the protection of clients' personally identifiable information (PII). Your company requires PII to be access controlled, encrypted, and compliant with major data protection standards. In addition to using Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP), you want to follow Google-recommended practices and use service accounts to control access to PII. What should you do?
answers: Assign the required Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles to every employee, and create a single service account to access project resources
Use one service account to access a Cloud SQL database, and use separate service accounts for each human user
Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use one service account shared by all users
Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use multiple service accounts attached to IAM groups to grant the appropriate access to each group
correct_answer: Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use multiple service accounts attached to IAM groups to grant the appropriate access to each group
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use multiple service accounts attached to IAM groups to grant the appropriate access to each group]**: Usar varias cuentas de servicio proporciona un control más granular y seguro. Los grupos IAM permiten gestionar permisos de manera eficiente, asegurando que solo los grupos adecuados tengan acceso a la información sensible.
- **:red[Assign the required Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles to every employee]**: Dar a todos los empleados los mismos permisos compromete la seguridad y es ineficiente.
- **:red[Use one service account to access a Cloud SQL database]**: Es ineficiente y genera problemas en la gestión de permisos.
- **:red[Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use one service account shared by all users]**: Compartir una sola cuenta de servicio conlleva riesgos de seguridad.

question: You need to migrate a Redis database from an on-premises data center to a Memorystore for Redis instance. You want to follow Google-recommended practices and perform the migration for minimal cost, time and effort. What should you do?
answers: Make an RDB backup of the Redis database, use the gsutil utility to copy the RDB file into a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import the RDB file into the Memorystore for Redis instance
Make a secondary instance of the Redis database on a Compute Engine instance and then perform a live cutover
Create a Dataflow job to read the Redis database from the on-premises data center and write the data to a Memorystore for Redis instance
Write a shell script to migrate the Redis data and create a new Memorystore for Redis instance
correct_answer: Make an RDB backup of the Redis database, use the gsutil utility to copy the RDB file into a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import the RDB file into the Memorystore for Redis instance
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Make an RDB backup of the Redis database, use the gsutil utility to copy the RDB file into a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import the RDB file into the Memorystore for Redis instance]**: Este método es eficiente, confiable y sigue las mejores prácticas recomendadas por Google para la migración de bases de datos Redis.
- **:red[Make a secondary instance of the Redis database on a Compute Engine instance]**: Es una opción más compleja y costosa en términos de tiempo y esfuerzo.
- **:red[Create a Dataflow job to read the Redis database]**: Dataflow es excesivamente complejo para una simple migración de Redis.
- **:red[Write a shell script to migrate the Redis data]**: Crear un script personalizado añade trabajo innecesario y puede ser menos confiable.

question: Your platform on your on-premises environment generates 100 GB of data daily, composed of millions of structured JSON text files. Your on-premises environment cannot be accessed from the public internet. You want to use Google Cloud products to query and explore the platform data. What should you do?
answers: Use Cloud Scheduler to copy data daily from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery
Use a Transfer Appliance to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery
Use Transfer Service for on-premises data to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery
Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service dataset copy to transfer all data into BigQuery
correct_answer: Use Transfer Service for on-premises data to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use Transfer Service for on-premises data to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery]**: Transfer Service es una opción escalable y segura para transferir grandes volúmenes de datos regularmente desde entornos on-premises.
- **:red[Use Cloud Scheduler]**: No es lo suficientemente eficiente para transferencias de grandes volúmenes de datos diarios.
- **:red[Use a Transfer Appliance]**: Adecuado para transferencias grandes iniciales, pero no para transferencias diarias.
- **:red[Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service dataset copy]**: No es eficiente para grandes volúmenes de datos estructurados como archivos JSON.

question: A TensorFlow machine learning model on Compute Engine virtual machines (n2-standard-32) takes two days to complete training. The model has custom TensorFlow operations that must run partially on a CPU. You want to reduce the training time in a cost-effective manner. What should you do?
answers: Change the VM type to n2-highmem-32
Change the VM type to e2-standard-32
Train the model using a VM with a GPU hardware accelerator
Train the model using a VM with a TPU hardware accelerator
correct_answer: Train the model using a VM with a GPU hardware accelerator
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Train the model using a VM with a GPU hardware accelerator]**: Las GPU están optimizadas para realizar operaciones paralelas, lo que acelera el entrenamiento de modelos de aprendizaje automático sin aumentar significativamente los costos.
- **:red[Change the VM type to n2-highmem-32]**: Aumentar la RAM no mejorará sustancialmente el rendimiento si el cuello de botella es el procesamiento.
- **:red[Change the VM type to e2-standard-32]**: Las VM e2 están diseñadas para cargas de trabajo de propósito general, no para tareas intensivas en computación como el aprendizaje automático.
- **:red[Train the model using a VM with a TPU hardware accelerator]**: Las TPU son poderosas pero más costosas y pueden no ser compatibles con todas las operaciones personalizadas en TensorFlow.

question: You want to create a machine learning model using BigQuery ML and create an endpoint for hosting the model using Vertex AI. This will enable the processing of continuous streaming data in near-real time from multiple vendors. The data may contain invalid values. What should you do?
answers: Create a new BigQuery dataset and use streaming inserts to land the data from multiple vendors. Configure your BigQuery ML model to use the 'ingestion' dataset as the framing data
Use BigQuery streaming inserts to land the data from multiple vendors where your BigQuery dataset ML model is deployed
Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Connect a Cloud Function to the topic to process the data and store it in BigQuery
Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Use Dataflow to process and sanitize the Pub/Sub data and stream it to BigQuery
correct_answer: Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Use Dataflow to process and sanitize the Pub/Sub data and stream it to BigQuery
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Use Dataflow to process and sanitize the Pub/Sub data and stream it to BigQuery]**: Pub/Sub y Dataflow son ideales para manejar flujos de datos en tiempo real, garantizando la limpieza y el procesamiento antes de almacenarlo en BigQuery.
- **:red[Create a new BigQuery dataset and use streaming inserts]**: No es ideal para gestionar datos sucios de múltiples fuentes en tiempo real.
- **:red[Use BigQuery streaming inserts]**: Usar inserts directos puede afectar el rendimiento del modelo y comprometer la calidad de los datos.
- **:red[Create a Pub/Sub topic and connect a Cloud Function]**: Aunque viable, las Cloud Functions no son tan escalables y eficientes para grandes volúmenes de datos como Dataflow.

question: You have a data processing application that runs on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Containers need to be launched with their latest available configurations from a container registry. Your GKE nodes need to have GPUs, local SSDs, and 8 Gbps bandwidth. You want to efficiently provision the data processing infrastructure and manage the deployment process. What should you do?
answers: Use Compute Engine startup scripts to pull container images, and use gcloud commands to provision the infrastructure
Use Cloud Build to schedule a job using Terraform build to provision the infrastructure and launch with the most current container images
Use GKE to autoscale containers, and use gcloud commands to provision the infrastructure
Use Dataflow to provision the data pipeline, and use Cloud Scheduler to run the job
correct_answer: Use Cloud Build to schedule a job using Terraform build to provision the infrastructure and launch with the most current container images
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use Cloud Build to schedule a job using Terraform build to provision the infrastructure and launch with the most current container images]**: Cloud Build permite automatizar el proceso de implementación y Terraform es la mejor herramienta para aprovisionar infraestructura de manera declarativa y eficiente.
- **:red[Use Compute Engine startup scripts]**: Usar scripts es menos eficiente y más propenso a errores que las soluciones automatizadas como Cloud Build y Terraform.
- **:red[Use GKE to autoscale containers]**: GKE permite la gestión de contenedores, pero no es adecuado para el aprovisionamiento de infraestructura de manera automatizada.
- **:red[Use Dataflow to provision the data pipeline]**: Dataflow es una plataforma para procesamiento de datos, no para la gestión de infraestructura o contenedores.

question: You need ads data to serve AI models and historical data for analytics. Longtail and outlier data points need to be identified. You want to cleanse the data in near-real time before running it through AI models. What should you do?
answers: Use Cloud Storage as a data warehouse, shell scripts for processing, and BigQuery to create views for desired datasets
Use Dataflow to identify longtail and outlier data points programmatically, with BigQuery as a sink
Use BigQuery to ingest, prepare, and then analyze the data, and then run queries to create views
Use Cloud Composer to identify longtail and outlier data points, and then output a usable dataset to BigQuery
correct_answer: Use Dataflow to identify longtail and outlier data points programmatically, with BigQuery as a sink
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Use Dataflow to identify longtail and outlier data points programmatically, with BigQuery as a sink]**: Dataflow permite el procesamiento de datos en tiempo real, lo que lo hace ideal para detectar puntos atípicos y datos de cola larga. Además, se integra con BigQuery para almacenar y analizar los datos procesados.
- **:red[Use Cloud Storage as a data warehouse]**: Cloud Storage no es una plataforma adecuada para procesamiento en tiempo real y el uso de shell scripts es propenso a errores.
- **:red[Use BigQuery to ingest, prepare, and then analyze the data]**: BigQuery es excelente para análisis, pero Dataflow es más adecuado para el procesamiento de datos en tiempo real.
- **:red[Use Cloud Composer to identify longtail and outlier data points]**: Cloud Composer es más útil para orquestar flujos de trabajo, no para procesar datos directamente.

question: You are collecting IoT sensor data from millions of devices across the world and storing the data in BigQuery. Your access pattern is based on recent data, filtered by location_id and device_version with the following query: SELECT Max(temperature) FROM acme_iot_dat.sensors WHERE Create_date>DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(),INTERVAL 7 day) AND location_id = 'SQ1W9TQ' AND device_version = '202007r3'. You want to optimize your queries for cost and performance. How should you structure your data?
answers: Partition table data by create_date, location_id, and device_version
Partition table data by create_date, cluster table data by location_id, and device_version
Cluster table data by create_date, location_id, and device_version
Cluster table data by create_date, partition by location_id, and device_version
correct_answer: Partition table data by create_date, cluster table data by location_id, and device_version
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Partition table data by create_date, cluster table data by location_id, and device_version]**: Particionar por fecha optimiza las consultas basadas en rango de fechas. Clusterizar por ubicación y versión mejora el rendimiento al agrupar los datos relacionados físicamente, lo que optimiza las consultas que filtran por estas columnas.
- **:red[Partition table data by create_date, location_id, and device_version]**: Particionar por múltiples columnas puede ser innecesario y costoso.
- **:red[Cluster table data by create_date, location_id, and device_version]**: Clusterizar por fecha no es eficiente, ya que los datos no relacionados se agruparían juntos.
- **:red[Cluster table data by create_date, partition by location_id, and device_version]**: Esto desorganiza los datos y no mejora el rendimiento.

question: A live TV show asks viewers to cast votes using their mobile phones. The event generates a large volume of data during a 3-minute period. You are in charge of the 'Voting infrastructure' and must ensure that the platform can handle the load and that all votes are processed. You must display partial results while voting is open. After voting closes, you need to count the votes exactly once while optimizing cost. What should you do?
answers: Create a Memorystore instance with a high availability (HA) configuration
Create a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database with high availability (HA) configuration and multiple read replicas
Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and have Cloud Functions subscribe to it and write votes to BigQuery

Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and load into both Bigtable and BigQuery via a Dataflow pipeline. Query Bigtable for real-time results and BigQuery for later analysis. Shut down the Bigtable instance when voting concludes
correct_answer: Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and load into both Bigtable and BigQuery via a Dataflow pipeline. Query Bigtable for real-time results and BigQuery for later analysis. Shut down the Bigtable instance when voting concludes
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and load into both Bigtable and BigQuery via a Dataflow pipeline]**: Pub/Sub maneja grandes volúmenes de datos en tiempo real. Bigtable es adecuado para consultas rápidas, mientras que BigQuery es excelente para análisis posteriores. Al cerrar la instancia de Bigtable al terminar la votación, optimizas el costo.
- **:red[Create a Memorystore instance with a high availability (HA) configuration]**: Memorystore no es adecuado para almacenar grandes volúmenes de datos durante un largo período.
- **:red[Create a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database with high availability (HA) configuration]**: Cloud SQL no es tan eficiente para manejar grandes volúmenes de datos en tiempo real como Bigtable.
- **:red[Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and have Cloud Functions subscribe to it]**: Cloud Functions puede no ser tan eficiente para manejar grandes volúmenes de datos como una combinación de Dataflow, Bigtable y BigQuery.

question: A shipping company has live package-tracking data that is sent to an Apache Kafka stream in real time. This is then loaded into BigQuery. Analysts in your company want to query the tracking data in BigQuery to analyze geospatial trends in the lifecycle of a package. The table was originally created with ingest-date partitioning. Over time, the query processing time has increased. You need to copy all the data to a new clustered table. What should you do?
answers: Re-create the table using data partitioning on the package delivery date
Implement clustering in BigQuery on the package-tracking ID column
Implement clustering in BigQuery on the ingest date column
Tier older data onto Cloud Storage files and create a BigQuery table using Cloud Storage as an external data source
correct_answer: Implement clustering in BigQuery on the package-tracking ID column
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Implement clustering in BigQuery on the package-tracking ID column]**: Clusterizar los datos por ID del paquete garantiza que los datos relacionados se almacenan físicamente juntos, mejorando el rendimiento en consultas de tendencias geoespaciales.
- **:red[Re-create the table using data partitioning on the package delivery date]**: No es óptimo, ya que los datos relacionados por ID pueden no estar juntos, lo que dificulta las consultas.
- **:red[Implement clustering in BigQuery on the ingest date column]**: Esto no ayuda a mejorar el rendimiento de consultas geoespaciales.
- **:red[Tier older data onto Cloud Storage]**: Puede ser ineficiente y dificulta el análisis en BigQuery.

question: You are designing a data mesh on Google Cloud with multiple distinct data engineering teams building data products. The typical data curation design pattern consists of landing files in Cloud Storage, transforming raw data in Cloud Storage and BigQuery datasets, and storing the final curated data product in BigQuery datasets. You need to configure Dataplex to ensure that each team can access only the assets needed to build their data products. You also need to ensure that teams can easily share the curated data product. What should you do?
answers: 1. Create a single Dataplex virtual lake and create a single zone to contain landing, raw, and curated data. 2. Provide each data engineering team access to the virtual lake

1. Create a single Dataplex virtual lake and create a single zone to contain landing, raw, and curated data. 2. Build separate assets for each data product within the zone. 3. Assign permissions to the data engineering teams at the zone level

1. Create a Dataplex virtual lake for each data product, and create a single zone to contain landing, raw, and curated data. 2. Provide the data engineering teams with full access to the virtual lake assigned to their data product

1. Create a Dataplex virtual lake for each data product, and create multiple zones for landing, raw, and curated data. 2. Provide the data engineering teams with full access to the virtual lake assigned to their data product
correct_answer: 1. Create a Dataplex virtual lake for each data product, and create multiple zones for landing, raw, and curated data. 2. Provide the data engineering teams with full access to the virtual lake assigned to their data product
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Create a Dataplex virtual lake for each data product, and create multiple zones for landing, raw, and curated data]**: Los virtual lakes y zonas separadas permiten un mejor control de acceso y organización por etapa de procesamiento, optimizando la gestión de datos y la colaboración entre equipos.
- **:red[Create a single Dataplex virtual lake and single zone]**: Tener un solo lake y zona puede complicar la gestión de acceso y control de los datos.
- **:red[Create a virtual lake for each product with a single zone]**: No dividir los datos en zonas separadas (landing, raw, curated) limita el control granular de los datos.
- **:red[Assign permissions at the zone level]**: Asignar permisos a nivel de zona es menos eficiente y menos seguro que asignar acceso por virtual lake.

question: You are using BigQuery with a multi-region dataset that includes a table with the daily sales volumes. This table is updated multiple times per day. You need to protect your sales table in case of regional failures with a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 24 hours, while keeping costs to a minimum. What should you do?
answers: Schedule a daily export of the table to a Cloud Storage dual or multi-region bucket
Schedule a daily copy of the dataset to a backup region
Schedule a daily BigQuery snapshot of the table
Modify ETL job to load the data into both the current and another backup region
correct_answer: Schedule a daily export of the table to a Cloud Storage dual or multi-region bucket
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Schedule a daily export of the table to a Cloud Storage dual or multi-region bucket]**: Cloud Storage multi-region buckets garantizan la disponibilidad de los datos en caso de fallas regionales y proporcionan redundancia sin aumentar significativamente los costos.
- **:red[Schedule a daily copy of the dataset to a backup region]**: Aunque ayuda, no ofrece la misma flexibilidad que Cloud Storage.
- **:red[Schedule a daily BigQuery snapshot of the table]**: Los snapshots no protegen contra fallas regionales de la misma manera.
- **:red[Modify ETL job to load data into both regions]**: Más complejo y menos eficiente que usar Cloud Storage.

question: You are troubleshooting your Dataflow pipeline that processes data from Cloud Storage to BigQuery. You have discovered that the Dataflow worker nodes cannot communicate with one another. Your networking team relies on Google Cloud network tags to define firewall rules. You need to identify the issue while following Google-recommended networking security practices. What should you do?
answers: Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline has a custom network tag set
Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 for the Dataflow network tag
Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 on the subnet used by Dataflow workers
Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline is deployed with the external IP address option enabled
correct_answer: Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 for the Dataflow network tag
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 for the Dataflow network tag]**: Los workers de Dataflow usan estos puertos para comunicarse, y la etiqueta de red controla el acceso a través de reglas de firewall.
- **:red[Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline has a custom network tag set]**: Las etiquetas de red se configuran automáticamente, no necesitan ser personalizadas.
- **:red[Determine whether there is a firewall rule for the subnet]**: La comunicación se gestiona a través de las etiquetas de red, no la subred.
- **:red[Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline uses an external IP]**: La IP externa no afecta la comunicación entre workers.

question: Your company's customer_order table in BigQuery stores the order history for 10 million customers, with a table size of 10 PB. You need to create a dashboard for the support team to view the order history. The dashboard has two filters, country_name and username. Both are string data types in the BigQuery table. When a filter is applied, the dashboard fetches the order history from the table and displays the query results. However, the dashboard is slow to show the results when applying the filters to the following query: SELECT date, order, status FROM customer_order WHERE country = '<country-name>' AND username = '<username>'. How should you redesign the BigQuery table to support faster access?
answers: Cluster the table by country and username fields
Cluster the table by country field, and partition by username field
Partition the table by country and username fields
Partition the table by _PARTITIONTIME
correct_answer: Cluster the table by country and username fields
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Cluster the table by country and username fields]**: Clusterizar por ambos campos asegura que los datos relacionados se almacenen juntos físicamente, mejorando el rendimiento de las consultas filtradas por estos campos.
- **:red[Cluster the table by country field, and partition by username field]**: Esto podría crear demasiadas particiones pequeñas y afectar el rendimiento.
- **:red[Partition the table by country and username fields]**: Particionar por ambos campos podría generar demasiadas particiones pequeñas, lo que sería ineficiente.
- **:red[Partition the table by _PARTITIONTIME]**: Esto no es relevante para consultas que no incluyen filtros basados en tiempo.

question: You have a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance deployed in a production environment. You need to simulate a Redis instance failover in the most accurate disaster recovery situation, and ensure that the failover has no impact on production data. What should you do?
answers: Create a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance in the development environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the limited-dataloss data protection mode
Create a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance in a development environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-dataloss data protection mode
Increase one replica to Redis instance in production environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-data-loss data protection mode
Initiate a manual failover by using the limited-data-loss data protection mode to the Memorystore for Redis instance in the production environment
correct_answer: Increase one replica to Redis instance in production environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-data-loss data protection mode
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Increase one replica to Redis instance in production environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-data-loss data protection mode]**: Crear una réplica adicional y realizar el failover asegura que la operación sea lo más precisa posible, sin impactar la producción.
- **:red[Create a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance in development]**: No refleja la realidad del entorno de producción.
- **:red[Initiate a manual failover by using the limited-data-loss mode]**: Sin una réplica adicional, esto podría afectar la disponibilidad del servicio en producción.

question: You are administering a BigQuery dataset that uses a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK). You need to share the dataset with a partner organization that does not have access to your CMEK. What should you do?
answers: Provide the partner organization a copy of your CMEKs to decrypt the data
Export the tables to parquet files to a Cloud Storage bucket and grant the storageinsights.viewer role on the bucket to the partner organization
Copy the tables you need to share to a dataset without CMEKs. Create an Analytics Hub listing for this dataset
Create an authorized view that contains the CMEK to decrypt the data when accessed
correct_answer: Copy the tables you need to share to a dataset without CMEKs. Create an Analytics Hub listing for this dataset
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Copy the tables to a dataset without CMEKs and create an Analytics Hub listing]**: Esta opción permite compartir datos sin necesidad de compartir la clave de cifrado, cumpliendo con los requisitos de seguridad.
- **:red[Provide the partner organization a copy of your CMEKs]**: Compartir la clave de cifrado es un riesgo de seguridad.
- **:red[Export the tables to parquet files]**: No es tan eficiente ni seguro como usar Analytics Hub.
- **:red[Create an authorized view with the CMEK]**: Esto no permite compartir los datos con seguridad adecuada.

question: You are developing an Apache Beam pipeline to extract data from a Cloud SQL instance by using JdbcIO. You have two projects running in Google Cloud. The pipeline will be deployed and executed on Dataflow in Project A. The Cloud SQL instance is running in Project B and does not have a public IP address. After deploying the pipeline, you noticed that the pipeline failed to extract data from the Cloud SQL instance due to connection failure. You verified that VPC Service Controls and shared VPC are not in use in these projects. You want to resolve this error while ensuring that the data does not go through the public internet. What should you do?
answers: Set up VPC Network Peering between Project A and Project B
Add a firewall rule to allow the peered subnet range to access all instances on the network
Turn off the external IP addresses on the Dataflow worker. Enable Cloud NAT in Project A

Set up VPC Network Peering between Project A and Project B. Create a Compute Engine instance without external IP address in Project B on the peered subnet to serve as a proxy server to the Cloud SQL database
correct_answer: Set up VPC Network Peering between Project A and Project B. Create a Compute Engine instance without external IP address in Project B on the peered subnet to serve as a proxy server to the Cloud SQL database
explanation:
- **✅:green[ VPC Network Peering with Compute Engine proxy]**: Esto permite una conexión segura entre los proyectos sin pasar por la Internet pública.
- **:red[Set up VPC Network Peering only]**: No resuelve el problema de acceso a una instancia sin IP pública.
- **:red[Turn off external IPs and enable Cloud NAT]**: Exponer las IPs públicas sigue representando un riesgo de seguridad.
- **:red[Add a firewall rule]**: No es suficiente para solucionar el problema.

question: You have a BigQuery table that contains customer data, including sensitive information such as names and addresses. You need to share the customer data with your data analytics and consumer support teams securely. The data analytics team needs to access the data of all the customers but must not be able to access the sensitive data. The consumer support team needs access to all data columns, but must not be able to access customers that no longer have active contracts. You enforced these requirements by using an authorized dataset and policy tags. After implementing these steps, the data analytics team reports that they still have access to the sensitive columns. You need to ensure that the data analytics team does not have access to restricted data. What should you do? (Choose two.)
answers: Create two separate authorized datasets; one for the data analytics team and another for the consumer support team
Ensure that the data analytics team members do not have the Data Catalog Fine-Grained Reader role for the policy tags
Replace the authorized dataset with an authorized view. Use row-level security and apply filter_expression to limit data access
Remove the bigquery.dataViewer role from the data analytics team on the authorized datasets
Enforce access control in the policy tag taxonomy
correct_answer: Ensure that the data analytics team members do not have the Data Catalog Fine-Grained Reader role for the policy tags
Enforce access control in the policy tag taxonomy
explanation:
- **✅:green[Ensure that the data analytics team members do not have the Data Catalog Fine-Grained Reader role for the policy tags]**: Esto garantiza que el equipo de análisis de datos no pueda ver las etiquetas de política que protegen los datos sensibles, impidiendo así el acceso no autorizado a columnas sensibles.

- **✅:green[Enforce access control in the policy tag taxonomy]**: Refuerza el control de acceso sobre las etiquetas de política para asegurar que las restricciones de acceso a los datos sensibles se apliquen correctamente.

- **:red[Create two separate authorized datasets]**: Añadir conjuntos de datos autorizados separados no resuelve el problema del acceso a columnas sensibles por parte del equipo de análisis de datos.

- **:red[Replace the authorized dataset with an authorized view]**: Esta opción podría ayudar con el acceso del equipo de soporte, pero no aborda directamente el problema del equipo de análisis de datos y el acceso a columnas sensibles.

- **:red[Remove the bigquery.dataViewer role]**: Eliminar el rol bigquery.dataViewer podría ser demasiado restrictivo, impidiendo que el equipo de análisis de datos realice su trabajo.

question: You have a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance in Region1 with one read replica in Region2 and another read replica in Region3. An unexpected event in Region1 requires that you perform disaster recovery by promoting a read replica in Region2. You need to ensure that your application has the same database capacity available before you switch over the connections. What should you do?
answers: Enable zonal high availability on the primary instance. Create a new read replica in a new region
Create a cascading read replica from the existing read replica in Region3
Create two new read replicas from the new primary instance, one in Region3 and one in a new region
Create a new read replica in Region1, promote the new read replica to be the primary instance, and enable zonal high availability
correct_answer: Create two new read replicas from the new primary instance, one in Region3 and one in a new region
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Create two new read replicas from the new primary instance]**: Esto asegura alta disponibilidad y capacidad adicional para evitar problemas en futuras fallas.
- **:red[Enable zonal high availability]**: Esto no resuelve el problema de disponibilidad interregional.
- **:red[Create a cascading read replica]**: No proporciona suficiente capacidad adicional.
- **:red[Create a new read replica in Region1]**: No mejora la tolerancia a fallos en diferentes regiones.

question: You orchestrate ETL pipelines by using Cloud Composer. One of the tasks in the Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) relies on a third-party service. You want to be notified when the task does not succeed. What should you do?
answers: Assign a function with notification logic to the on_retry_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk
Configure a Cloud Monitoring alert on the sla_missed metric associated with the task at risk to trigger a notification
Assign a function with notification logic to the on_failure_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk
Assign a function with notification logic to the sla_miss_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk
correct_answer: Assign a function with notification logic to the on_failure_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Assign a function with notification logic to the on_failure_callback parameter]**: Este parámetro se activa cuando una tarea falla completamente, permitiendo notificar de manera eficiente sobre el problema.
- **:red[Assign a function with notification logic to the on_retry_callback]**: Solo se activa cuando una tarea se reintenta, no cuando falla.
- **:red[Configure a Cloud Monitoring alert]**: Cloud Monitoring puede detectar fallos, pero no es tan flexible como una función personalizada.
- **:red[Assign a function with notification logic to the sla_miss_callback]**: Este parámetro se activa cuando una tarea no cumple con los SLA, pero no es tan útil para detectar fallos en servicios externos.

question: You are migrating your on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. One of the upstream data sources resides on a MySQL database that runs in your on-premises data center with no public IP addresses. You want to ensure that the data ingestion into BigQuery is done securely and does not go through the public internet. What should you do?
answers: Update your existing on-premises ETL tool to write to BigQuery by using the BigQuery Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver. Set up the proxy parameter in the simba.googlebigqueryodbc.ini file to point to your data center’s NAT gateway

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Set up Cloud Interconnect between your on-premises data center and Google Cloud. Use Private connectivity as the connectivity method and allocate an IP address range within your VPC network to the Datastream connectivity configuration. Use Server-only as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Use Forward-SSH tunnel as the connectivity method to establish a secure tunnel between Datastream and your on-premises MySQL database through a tunnel server in your on-premises data center. Use None as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Gather Datastream public IP addresses of the Google Cloud region that will be used to set up the stream. Add those IP addresses to the firewall allowlist of your on-premises data center. Use IP Allowlisting as the connectivity method and Server-only as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream
correct_answer: Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Set up Cloud Interconnect between your on-premises data center and Google Cloud. Use Private connectivity as the connectivity method and allocate an IP address range within your VPC network to the Datastream connectivity configuration. Use Server-only as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream
explanation:
- **✅:green[ Datastream with Cloud Interconnect and private connectivity]**: Este enfoque asegura que los datos se transfieren de forma privada y segura sin pasar por la Internet pública.
- **:red[Update your existing ETL tool]**: Esto puede ser menos eficiente y seguro que usar Datastream.
- **:red[Use Forward-SSH tunnel]**: Aunque seguro, puede ser más complejo de configurar que Cloud Interconnect.
- **:red[Use IP Allowlisting]**: Permitir IPs públicas puede representar un riesgo de seguridad.

question: You store and analyze your relational data in BigQuery on Google Cloud with all data that resides in US regions. You also have a variety of object stores across Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS), also in US regions. You want to query all your data in BigQuery daily with as little movement of data as possible. What should you do?
answers: Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to load files from Azure and AWS into BigQuery
Create a Dataflow pipeline to ingest files from Azure and AWS to BigQuery
Load files from AWS and Azure to Cloud Storage with Cloud Shell gsutil rsync arguments
Use the BigQuery Omni functionality and BigLake tables to query files in Azure and AWS
correct_answer: Use the BigQuery Omni functionality and BigLake tables to query files in Azure and AWS
explanation:
- **✅:green[ BigQuery Omni and BigLake tables]**: Esto permite consultar datos directamente en su ubicación sin moverlos, optimizando costos y evitando el movimiento de datos.
- **:red[Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service]**: Esto implica mover los datos a BigQuery, lo que no es eficiente.
- **:red[Create a Dataflow pipeline]**: Involucra la transferencia de datos, lo que no es necesario con BigQuery Omni.
- **:red[Load files from AWS and Azure to Cloud Storage]**: Mover los datos a Cloud Storage no es la opción más eficiente cuando BigQuery Omni puede consultar los datos directamente.

question: You have a variety of files in Cloud Storage that your data science team wants to use in their models. Currently, users do not have a method to explore, cleanse, and validate the data in Cloud Storage. You are looking for a low-code solution that can be used by your data science team to quickly cleanse and explore data within Cloud Storage. What should you do?
answers: Provide the data science team access to Dataflow to create a pipeline to prepare and validate the raw data and load data into BigQuery for data exploration
Create an external table in BigQuery and use SQL to transform the data as necessary. Provide the data science team Access to the external tables to explore the raw data
Load the data into BigQuery and use SQL to transform the data as necessary. Provide the data science team access to staging tables to explore the raw data
Provide the data science team access to Dataprep to prepare, validate, and explore the data within Cloud Storage
correct_answer: Provide the data science team access to Dataprep to prepare, validate, and explore the data within Cloud Storage
explanation:
- **✅:green[Provide the data science team access to Dataprep to prepare, validate, and explore the data within Cloud Storage]**: Dataprep permite realizar operaciones de limpieza, transformación y exploración de datos sin necesidad de escribir código. Es una solución perfecta para equipos que necesitan una herramienta de bajo código.
- **:red[Provide the data science team access to Dataflow]**: Dataflow requiere conocimientos de programación y no es una solución low-code.
- **:red[Create an external table in BigQuery]**: Usar SQL para transformación no es ideal para la exploración de datos sin conocimientos técnicos avanzados.
- **:red[Load the data into BigQuery]**: Tampoco es una solución low-code ya que requiere usar SQL para transformar datos.

question: You are building an ELT solution in BigQuery by using Dataform. You need to perform uniqueness and null value checks on your final tables. What should you do to efficiently integrate these checks into your pipeline?
answers: Build BigQuery user-defined functions (UDFs)
Create Dataplex data quality tasks
Build Dataform assertions into your code
Write a Spark-based stored procedure
correct_answer: Build Dataform assertions into your code
explanation:
- **✅:green[Build Dataform assertions into your code]**: Dataform permite incluir assertions directamente en el código SQL para realizar chequeos como la unicidad o valores nulos. Es eficiente y fácil de mantener.
- **:red[Build BigQuery user-defined functions (UDFs)]**: Las UDFs son para reutilizar lógica o cálculos, no para validación de calidad de datos.
- **:red[Create Dataplex data quality tasks]**: Dataplex es una solución más compleja y no es ideal para chequeos simples en pipelines de Dataform.
- **:red[Write a Spark-based stored procedure]**: Agregaría demasiada complejidad innecesaria al pipeline de BigQuery.

question: A web server sends click events to a Pub/Sub topic as messages. The web server includes an eventTimestamp attribute in the messages, which is the time when the click occurred. You have a Dataflow streaming job that reads from this Pub/Sub topic through a subscription, applies some transformations, and writes the result to another Pub/Sub topic for use by the advertising department. The advertising department needs to receive each message within 30 seconds of the corresponding click occurrence, but they report receiving the messages late. Your Dataflow job's system lag is about 5 seconds, and the data freshness is about 40 seconds. Inspecting a few messages show no more than 1 second lag between their eventTimestamp and publishTime. What is the problem and what should you do?
answers: The advertising department is causing delays when consuming the messages. Work with the advertising department to fix this
Messages in your Dataflow job are taking more than 30 seconds to process. Optimize your job or increase the number of workers to fix this

Messages in your Dataflow job are processed in less than 30 seconds, but your job cannot keep up with the backlog in the Pub/Sub subscription. Optimize your job or increase the number of workers to fix this
The web server is not pushing messages fast enough to Pub/Sub. Work with the web server team to fix this
correct_answer: Messages in your Dataflow job are processed in less than 30 seconds, but your job cannot keep up with the backlog in the Pub/Sub subscription. Optimize your job or increase the number of workers to fix this
explanation:
- **✅:green[Messages in your Dataflow job are processed in less than 30 seconds, but your job cannot keep up with the backlog in the Pub/Sub subscription]**: Dataflow está procesando correctamente pero no puede seguir el ritmo del volumen de mensajes, lo que indica una acumulación. Incrementar el número de workers o optimizar el pipeline solucionaría este problema.
- **:red[The advertising department is causing delays]**: No es correcto ya que los retrasos ocurren antes de que lleguen al departamento de publicidad.
- **:red[Messages in your Dataflow job are taking more than 30 seconds to process]**: El lag del sistema es de solo 5 segundos, no es el procesamiento de los mensajes lo que está causando el problema.
- **:red[The web server is not pushing messages fast enough]**: Esto no es cierto ya que hay solo 1 segundo de lag entre el eventTimestamp y publishTime.

question: Your organization stores customer data in an on-premises Apache Hadoop cluster in Apache Parquet format. Data is processed on a daily basis by Apache Spark jobs that run on the cluster. You are migrating the Spark jobs and Parquet data to Google Cloud. BigQuery will be used on future transformation pipelines so you need to ensure that your data is available in BigQuery. You want to use managed services, while minimizing ETL data processing changes and overhead costs. What should you do?
answers: Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and migrate the metadata to Dataproc Metastore (DPMS). Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc Serverless
Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and register the bucket as a Dataplex asset. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc Serverless
Migrate your data to BigQuery. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on BigQuery, and run them on Dataproc Serverless
Migrate your data to BigLake. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc on Compute Engine
correct_answer: Migrate your data to BigQuery. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on BigQuery, and run them on Dataproc Serverless
explanation:
- **✅:green[Migrate your data to BigQuery]**: Migrar los datos a BigQuery asegura que estén disponibles para su procesamiento inmediato y se integren fácilmente con futuras canalizaciones de transformación.
- **:red[Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and migrate the metadata to Dataproc Metastore]**: No permite acceso inmediato a BigQuery sin configuración adicional.
- **:red[Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and register the bucket as a Dataplex asset]**: Introduce complejidad innecesaria comparado con migrar directamente a BigQuery.
- **:red[Migrate your data to BigLake]**: Es más complejo de gestionar y requiere configuración adicional para asegurar la disponibilidad en BigQuery.

question: Your organization has two Google Cloud projects, project A and project B. In project A, you have a Pub/Sub topic that receives data from confidential sources. Only the resources in project A should be able to access the data in that topic. You want to ensure that project B and any future project cannot access data in the project A topic. What should you do?
answers: Add firewall rules in project A so only traffic from the VPC in Project A is permitted
Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around Project A
Use Identity and Access Management conditions to ensure that only users and service accounts in project A. can access resources in Project A
Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around the VPC of Project A
correct_answer: Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around Project A
explanation:
- **✅:green[Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around Project A]**: Los controles de servicio VPC permiten definir perímetros de seguridad que restringen el acceso a los recursos, asegurando que solo los recursos dentro del perímetro puedan acceder al tema de Pub/Sub.
- **:red[Add firewall rules in project A]**: Controla el tráfico de red pero no el acceso a Pub/Sub, lo que no es suficiente.
- **:red[Use Identity and Access Management conditions]**: IAM maneja permisos de usuario pero no crea perímetros efectivos para proteger todos los recursos.
- **:red[Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around the VPC of Project A]**: Esto asegura la red, pero no controla los recursos de Pub/Sub.

question: You stream order data by using a Dataflow pipeline, and write the aggregated result to Memorystore. You provisioned a Memorystore for Redis instance with Basic Tier, 4 GB capacity, which is used by 40 clients for read-only access. You are expecting the number of read-only clients to increase significantly to a few hundred and you need to be able to support the demand. You want to ensure that read and write access availability is not impacted, and any changes you make can be deployed quickly. What should you do?
answers: Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 4 GB and read replica to No read replicas (high availability only). Delete the old instance
Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 5 GB and create multiple read replicas. Delete the old instance

Create a new Memorystore for Memcached instance. Set a minimum of three nodes, and memory per node to 4 GB. Modify the Dataflow pipeline and all clients to use the Memcached instance. Delete the old instance
Create multiple new Memorystore for Redis instances with Basic Tier (4 GB capacity). Modify the Dataflow pipeline and new clients to use all instances
correct_answer: Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 5 GB and create multiple read replicas. Delete the old instance
explanation:
- **✅:green[Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 5 GB and create multiple read replicas]**: Las réplicas de lectura permiten escalar para manejar más clientes, mientras que el Standard Tier asegura alta disponibilidad.
- **:red[Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 4 GB and read replica to No read replicas (high availability only). Delete the old instance]**: No ofrece la escalabilidad adicional que las réplicas de lectura proporcionan.
- **:red[Create a new Memorystore for Memcached instance]**: Requiere modificar el pipeline y todos los clientes, lo cual no es rápido.
- **:red[Create multiple new Memorystore for Redis instances]**: No proporciona alta disponibilidad y requeriría una modificación considerable del pipeline.

question: You have a streaming pipeline that ingests data from Pub/Sub in production. You need to update this streaming pipeline with improved business logic. You need to ensure that the updated pipeline reprocesses the previous two days of delivered Pub/Sub messages. What should you do? (Choose two.)
answers: Use the Pub/Sub subscription clear-retry-policy flag
Use Pub/Sub Snapshot capture two days before the deployment
Create a new Pub/Sub subscription two days before the deployment
Use the Pub/Sub subscription retain-acked-messages flag
Use Pub/Sub Seek with a timestamp
correct_answer: Use the Pub/Sub subscription retain-acked-messages flag
Use Pub/Sub Seek with a timestamp
explanation:
- **✅:green[Use Pub/Sub Seek with a timestamp]**: Permite reprocesar mensajes antiguos moviendo el cursor de la suscripción a un punto específico en el tiempo.
- **✅:green[Use the Pub/Sub subscription retain-acked-messages flag]**: Esto asegura que los mensajes reconocidos anteriormente sean retenidos para poder ser reprocesados.
- **:red[Use the Pub/Sub subscription clear-retry-policy flag]**: No recupera mensajes antiguos.
- **:red[Use Pub/Sub Snapshot]**: Requiere planificación previa que no fue mencionada en el caso.
- **:red[Create a new Pub/Sub subscription]**: No permitirá acceder a los mensajes publicados antes de la creación de la suscripción.

question: You currently use a SQL-based tool to visualize your data stored in BigQuery. The data visualizations require the use of outer joins and analytic functions. Visualizations must be based on data that is no less than 4 hours old. Business users are complaining that the visualizations are too slow to generate. You want to improve the performance of the visualization queries while minimizing the maintenance overhead of the data preparation pipeline. What should you do?
answers: Create materialized views with the allow_non_incremental_definition option set to true for the visualization queries. Specify the max_staleness parameter to 4 hours and the enable_refresh parameter to true. Reference the materialized views in the data visualization tool
Create views for the visualization queries. Reference the views in the data visualization tool

Create a Cloud Function instance to export the visualization query results as parquet files to a Cloud Storage bucket. Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger the Cloud Function every 4 hours. Reference the parquet files in the data visualization tool

Create materialized views for the visualization queries. Use the incremental updates capability of BigQuery materialized views to handle changed data automatically. Reference the materialized views in the data visualization tool
correct_answer: Create materialized views with the allow_non_incremental_definition option set to true for the visualization queries. Specify the max_staleness parameter to 4 hours and the enable_refresh parameter to true. Reference the materialized views in the data visualization tool
explanation:
- **✅:green[Create materialized views with the allow_non_incremental_definition option set to true for the visualization queries]**: Las vistas materializadas almacenan resultados precomputados de consultas complejas y estableciendo el parámetro max_staleness a 4 horas garantiza que las visualizaciones utilicen datos actualizados. 
- **:red[Create views for the visualization queries]**: Las vistas estándar no mejoran significativamente el rendimiento porque no almacenan resultados precomputados.
- **:red[Create a Cloud Function instance]**: Esta opción aumenta el mantenimiento, ya que involucra Cloud Functions y Cloud Scheduler para la ejecución periódica.
- **:red[Create materialized views for the visualization queries]**: Las actualizaciones incrementales no son adecuadas para consultas que requieren joins externos y funciones analíticas complejas.

question: You need to modernize your existing on-premises data strategy. Your organization currently uses: • Apache Hadoop clusters for processing multiple large data sets, including on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) for data replication. • Apache Airflow to orchestrate hundreds of ETL pipelines with thousands of job steps. You need to set up a new architecture in Google Cloud that can handle your Hadoop workloads and requires minimal changes to your existing orchestration processes. What should you do?
answers: Use Bigtable for your large workloads, with connections to Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Orchestrate your pipelines with Cloud Composer
Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Orchestrate your pipelines with Cloud Composer
Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Convert your ETL pipelines to Dataflow
Use Dataproc to migrate your Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Use Cloud Data Fusion to visually design and deploy your ETL pipelines
correct_answer: Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Orchestrate your pipelines with Cloud Composer
explanation:
- **✅:green[Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases]**: Dataproc es una solución gestionada que permite ejecutar clústeres de Hadoop en Google Cloud sin necesidad de rediseñar los flujos de trabajo existentes. Además, Cloud Storage sustituye efectivamente a HDFS, y Cloud Composer es compatible con Apache Airflow, permitiendo cambios mínimos en la orquestación.
- **:red[Use Bigtable for your large workloads]**: Bigtable no es adecuado para migrar Hadoop y requiere rediseño.
- **:red[Convert your ETL pipelines to Dataflow]**: Convertir los pipelines ETL a Dataflow implicaría una reescritura significativa.
- **:red[Use Cloud Data Fusion]**: Migrar pipelines a Cloud Data Fusion implicaría cambios considerables en la orquestación.

question: You recently deployed several data processing jobs into your Cloud Composer 2 environment. You notice that some tasks are failing in Apache Airflow. On the monitoring dashboard, you see an increase in the total workers memory usage, and there were worker pod evictions. You need to resolve these errors. What should you do? (Choose two.)
answers: Increase the directed acyclic graph (DAG) file parsing Interval
Increase the Cloud Composer 2 environment size from médium to large
Increase the maximum number of workers and reduce worker concurrency
Increase the memory available to the Airflow workers
Increase the memory available to the Airflow triggerer
correct_answer: Increase the maximum number of workers and reduce worker concurrency
Increase the memory available to the Airflow workers
explanation:
- **✅:green[Increase the maximum number of workers and reduce worker concurrency]**: Esto permite que los trabajadores manejen menos tareas simultáneamente, lo que reduce el uso de memoria y mejora la estabilidad del entorno.
- **✅:green[Increase the memory available to the Airflow workers]**: Aumentar la memoria de los trabajadores evitará problemas relacionados con la falta de recursos.
- **:red[Increase the directed acyclic graph (DAG) file parsing Interval]**: No resuelve problemas de memoria.
- **:red[Increase the Cloud Composer 2 environment size]**: Aumentar el tamaño del entorno no optimiza el uso de los recursos.
- **:red[Increase the memory available to the Airflow triggerer]**: No aborda el problema de uso de memoria de los trabajadores.

question: You are on the data governance team and are implementing security requirements to deploy resources. You need to ensure that resources are limited to only the europe-west3 region. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
answers: Set the constraints/gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint to in\:europe-west3-locations
Deploy resources with Terraform and implement a variable validation rule to ensure that the region is set to the europe-west3 region for all resources
Set the constraints/gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint to in\:eu-locations
Create a Cloud Function to monitor all resources created and automatically destroy the ones created outside the europe-west3 region
correct_answer: Set the constraints/gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint to in\:europe-west3-locations
explanation:
- **✅:green[Set the constraints/gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint to in\:europe-west3-locations]**: Esto garantiza que todos los recursos estén limitados a la región europe-west3, siguiendo las mejores prácticas recomendadas por Google para limitar las ubicaciones de recursos.
- **:red[Deploy resources with Terraform and implement a variable validation rule]**: Terraform no ofrece garantías centralizadas y organizativas para restringir las creaciones de recursos.
- **:red[Set the constraints/gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint to in\:eu-locations]**: Esto permitiría el despliegue en cualquier región de la Unión Europea, no solo en europe-west3.
- **:red[Create a Cloud Function to monitor all resources]**: Este enfoque es reactivo y conlleva riesgos de destrucción automática de recursos.

question: You are a BigQuery admin supporting a team of data consumers who run ad hoc queries and downstream reporting in tools such as Looker. All data and users are combined under a single organizational project. You recently noticed some slowness in query results and want to troubleshoot where the slowdowns are occurring. You think that there might be some job queuing or slot contention occurring as users run jobs, which slows down access to results. You need to investigate the query job information and determine where performance is being affected. What should you do?
answers: Use slot reservations for your project to ensure that you have enough query processing capacity and are able to allocate available slots to the slower queries
Use Cloud Monitoring to view BigQuery metrics and set up alerts that let you know when a certain percentage of slots were used
Use available administrative resource charts to determine how slots are being used and how jobs are performing over time. Run a query on the INFORMATION_SCHEMA to review query performance
Use Cloud Logging to determine if any users or downstream consumers are changing or deleting access grants on tagged resources
correct_answer: Use available administrative resource charts to determine how slots are being used and how jobs are performing over time. Run a query on the INFORMATION_SCHEMA to review query performance
explanation:
- **✅:green[Use available administrative resource charts to determine how slots are being used]**: Estos gráficos permiten ver el uso de slots y cómo rinden los trabajos a lo largo del tiempo, identificando cuellos de botella. Además, INFORMATION_SCHEMA proporciona información detallada sobre el rendimiento de las consultas.
- **:red[Use slot reservations]**: Aunque útil, primero se debe investigar si hay problemas con la contención de slots.
- **:red[Use Cloud Monitoring]**: Monitorea métricas en tiempo real, pero no proporciona detalles históricos para investigar el rendimiento.
- **:red[Use Cloud Logging]**: Es más adecuado para auditorías de seguridad, no para el análisis de rendimiento de consultas.

question: You migrated a data backend for an application that serves 10 PB of historical product data for analytics. Only the last known state for a product, which is about 10 GB of data, needs to be served through an API to the other applications. You need to choose a cost-effective persistent storage solution that can accommodate the analytics requirements and the API performance of up to 1000 queries per second (QPS) with less than 1 second latency. What should you do?
answers: Store the historical data in BigQuery for analytics. Use a materialized view to precompute the last state of a product. Serve the last state data directly from BigQuery to the API

Store the products as a collection in Firestore with each product having a set of historical changes. Use simple and compound queries for analytics. Serve the last state data directly from Firestore to the API
Store the historical data in Cloud SQL for analytics. In a separate table, store the last state of the product after every product change. Serve the last state data directly from Cloud SQL to the API
Store the historical data in BigQuery for analytics. In a Cloud SQL table, store the last state of the product after every product change. Serve the last state data directly from Cloud SQL to the API
correct_answer: Store the historical data in BigQuery for analytics. In a Cloud SQL table, store the last state of the product after every product change. Serve the last state data directly from Cloud SQL to the API
explanation:
- **✅:green[Store the historical data in BigQuery for analytics. In a Cloud SQL table, store the last state of the product]**: BigQuery es excelente para manejar los 10 PB de datos históricos, mientras que Cloud SQL es ideal para manejar los 10 GB de datos actuales del producto con baja latencia y alto rendimiento en consultas API.
- **:red[Store the historical data in BigQuery for analytics]**: BigQuery no es adecuado para consultas de alta frecuencia y baja latencia para una API de alto rendimiento.
- **:red[Store the products as a collection in Firestore]**: Firestore no es adecuado para manejar 10 PB de datos históricos.
- **:red[Store the historical data in Cloud SQL]**: Almacenar 10 PB de datos históricos en Cloud SQL no es práctico ni rentable.

question: You want to schedule a number of sequential load and transformation jobs. Data files will be added to a Cloud Storage bucket by an upstream process. There is no fixed schedule for when the new data arrives. Next, a Dataproc job is triggered to perform some transformations and write the data to BigQuery. You then need to run additional transformation jobs in BigQuery. The transformation jobs are different for every table. These jobs might take hours to complete. You need to determine the most efficient and maintainable workflow to process hundreds of tables and provide the freshest data to your end users. What should you do?
answers: Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Cloud Storage, Dataproc, and BigQuery operators. Use a single shared DAG for all tables that need to go through the pipeline. Schedule the DAG to run hourly

Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Cloud Storage, Dataproc, and BigQuery operators. Create a separate DAG for each table that needs to go through the pipeline. Schedule the DAGs to run hourly

Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Dataproc and BigQuery operators. Use a single shared DAG for all tables that need to go through the pipeline. Use a Cloud Storage object trigger to launch a Cloud Function that triggers the DAG

Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Dataproc and BigQuery operators. Create a separate DAG for each table that needs to go through the pipeline. Use a Cloud Storage object trigger to launch a Cloud Function that triggers the DAG
correct_answer: Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Dataproc and BigQuery operators. Create a separate DAG for each table that needs to go through the pipeline. Use a Cloud Storage object trigger to launch a Cloud Function that triggers the DAG
explanation:
